label: Teltonika TSW100
description: A five-port industrial Gigabit switch with PoE+ on four of them: the fifth port is the uplink, the other four power cameras and access points.
notes: Vendor figures (Teltonika wiki): 5 x Gigabit Ethernet ports, 4 of which can power connected devices via PoE 802.3af/802.3at. eth0 is modelled without PoE because the vendor says four of the five ports are PoE-capable; the fifth is the uplink. PSE CENSUS: eth0 is declared `"poeOut": false` because the vendor names the PoE sockets "Port 1- 4" and the fifth as the uplink (the datasheet's own installation drawing: "Connect your main internet router/modem to TSW100 LAN port number 5"). Left undeclared, the engine's best-effort inference gave this copper port 15.4 W of 802.3af - a fifth outlet the box does not have, and now that a 120 W budget exists, one that could fund a powered device from the uplink.

poe.note: Datasheet (TSW100, 2023-v1.3), POE block, verbatim: "PoE ports Port 1- 4"; "PoE standards 802.3af and 802.3at"; "PoE Max Power per Port (at PSE) 30 W"; "PoE Power Budget (at PSE) 120 W"; "Power consumption Idle: 2 W / Max (no PoE): 9 W / PoE Max: 129 W". Four 30 W ports at full fill are exactly 120 W, so the budget and the port ceilings meet with nothing to spare - the 120 W row is what decides a fifth device, not the per-port figure. Read 2026-11-20; the 120 W headline is on the product page too ("Total power budget at PSE up to 120 W", https://teltonika-networks.com/products/switches/tsw100). NOT MODELLED, and why this matters to a lab: the switch is bundled with a 48 V / 1.3 A adapter (62.4 W), and the datasheet footnote says "Provided power supply only allows 60 W PoE power budget at PSE, to reach maximum 120 W at PSE >130 W power supply must be used" - 120 W is the chassis ceiling at PSE, 60 W is what the box in the carton can do. This simulator models the chassis (its power source is not a field), so the bill of materials is recorded here rather than compiled in.
